subject: Query Regarding Bayesian Generalized Linear Mixed Effects Model with Spatiotemporal Covariance Structure Using INLA

messages.author: 9ac3aea83233f083
messages.subject: Query Regarding Bayesian Generalized Linear Mixed Effects Model with Spatiotemporal Covariance Structure Using INLA
parts:
Dear INLA community,
I am currently working on establishing a Bayesian generalized linear mixed effects model with a spatiotemporal covariance structure using the INLA package in R. My dataset has a non-temporal structure, meaning that the number and location of observation sites vary each year. To accommodate this variability, I have considered converting the data into panel format, generating dependent variable observations for all years from 2000 to 2019 and filling missing values with NA.
Here is my code:

stk.e <- inla.stack(
  tag = "est",
  data = list(y = C_Y_T$Y),
  A = list(1, A_SAM),
  effects = list(data.frame(b0 = 1, X1=C_Y_T$ID), s = w.index)
)

rprior1 <- list(theta = list(prior = 'loggamma', param = c(1, 0.02)), theta1 = list(prior = 'normal', param = c(0, 1/(2^2))))
formula <- y ~ X1 + f(w, model = spde.sp, group = w.group, control.group = list(model = "ar1", hyper = rprior1))

res <- inla(formula,
            family = "gaussian",
            data = inla.stack.data(stk.e),
            control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk.e), compute = TRUE),
            control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, config = TRUE),
            control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb"),
            verbose = TRUE
)

When I run the code, I received the warnings and errors:



My question is whether the INLA model can handle such a dataset with missing values (NA) appropriately, or if it will automatically remove these missing values during the model fitting process. I would like to understand whether INLA can deal with datasets where the observation sites are not consistent across time points and how this might affect the model's performance and results.

Any help will be greatly appreciated.

Best wishes,
